5: 
6: # Sandbox Agent
7: 
8: Sandbox Agent provides a universal API for orchestrating AI coding agents in sandboxed environments.
9: 
10: ## What To Do If You Get Stuck
11: 
12: If something is not working as intended or you are stuck, prompt the user to join the [Rivet Discord](https://rivet.dev/discord) or file an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/rivet-dev/sandbox-agent/issues) to report an issue and get help.
13: 
14: Provide the user with a pre-generated report with:
15: 
16: - Symptoms
17: 	- If this is happening in local dev, deployed, or both
18: 	- The error you're seeing
19: 	- Relevant source code related to this
20: - What you've tried to solve it
21: - Environment
22: 	- Sandbox Agent version
23: 	- SDK in use (TypeScript, Python, or HTTP)
24: 	- Agent in use (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Amp, Mock)
25: 	- Sandbox provider (E2B, Daytona, Docker, local)
26: 
27: ## Quickstart
28: 
29: ### Install skill (optional)
30: 
31: #### npx
32: 
33: ```bash
34: npx skills add rivet-dev/skills -s sandbox-agent
35: ```
36: 
37: #### bunx
38: 
39: ```bash
40: bunx skills add rivet-dev/skills -s sandbox-agent
41: ```
42: 
43: ### Set environment variables
44: 
45: Each coding agent requires API keys to connect to their respective LLM providers.
46: 
47: #### Local shell
48: 
49: ```bash
50: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
51: export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
52: ```
53: 
54: #### E2B
55: 
56: ```typescript
57: import { Sandbox } from "@e2b/code-interpreter";
58: 
59: const envs: Record<string, string> = {};
60: if (process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) envs.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;
61: if (process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) envs.OPENAI_API_KEY = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
62: 
63: const sandbox = await Sandbox.create({ envs });
64: ```
65: 
66: #### Daytona
67: 
68: ```typescript
69: import { Daytona } from "@daytonaio/sdk";
70: 
71: const envVars: Record<string, string> = {};
72: if (process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) envVars.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;
73: if (process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) envVars.OPENAI_API_KEY = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
74: 
75: const daytona = new Daytona();
76: const sandbox = await daytona.create({
77:   snapshot: "sandbox-agent-ready",
78:   envVars,
79: });
80: ```
81: 
82: #### Docker
83: 
84: ```bash
85: docker run -p 2468:2468 \
86:   -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." \
87:   -e OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." \
88:   rivetdev/sandbox-agent:0.4.2-full \
89:   server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
90: ```
91: 
92: #### Extracting API keys from current machine
93: 
94: Use `sandbox-agent credentials extract-env --export` to extract your existing API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) from local Claude Code or Codex config files.
95: 
96: #### Testing without API keys
97: 
98: Use the `mock` agent for SDK and integration testing without provider credentials.
99: 
100: #### Multi-tenant and per-user billing
101: 
102: For per-tenant token tracking, budget enforcement, or usage-based billing, see [LLM Credentials](/llm-credentials) for gateway options like OpenRouter, LiteLLM, and Portkey.
103: 
104: ### Run the server
105: 
106: #### curl
107: 
108: Install and run the binary directly.
109: 
110: ```bash
111: curl -fsSL https://releases.rivet.dev/sandbox-agent/0.4.x/install.sh | sh
112: sandbox-agent server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
113: ```
114: 
115: #### npx
116: 
117: Run without installing globally.
118: 
119: ```bash
120: npx @sandbox-agent/cli@0.4.x server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
121: ```
122: 
123: #### bunx
124: 
125: Run without installing globally.
126: 
127: ```bash
128: bunx @sandbox-agent/cli@0.4.x server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
129: ```
130: 
131: #### npm i -g
132: 
133: Install globally, then run.
134: 
135: ```bash
136: npm install -g @sandbox-agent/cli@0.4.x
137: sandbox-agent server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
138: ```
139: 
140: #### bun add -g
141: 
142: Install globally, then run.
143: 
144: ```bash
145: bun add -g @sandbox-agent/cli@0.4.x
146: # Allow Bun to run postinstall scripts for native binaries (required for SandboxAgent.start()).
147: bun pm -g trust @sandbox-agent/cli-linux-x64 @sandbox-agent/cli-linux-arm64 @sandbox-agent/cli-darwin-arm64 @sandbox-agent/cli-darwin-x64 @sandbox-agent/cli-win32-x64
148: sandbox-agent server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
149: ```
150: 
151: #### Node.js (local)
152: 
153: For local development, use `SandboxAgent.start()` to spawn and manage the server as a subprocess.
154: 
155: ```bash
156: npm install sandbox-agent@0.4.x
157: ```
158: 
159: ```typescript
160: import { SandboxAgent } from "sandbox-agent";
161: 
162: const sdk = await SandboxAgent.start();
163: ```
164: 
165: #### Bun (local)
166: 
167: For local development, use `SandboxAgent.start()` to spawn and manage the server as a subprocess.
168: 
169: ```bash
170: bun add sandbox-agent@0.4.x
171: # Allow Bun to run postinstall scripts for native binaries (required for SandboxAgent.start()).
172: bun pm trust @sandbox-agent/cli-linux-x64 @sandbox-agent/cli-linux-arm64 @sandbox-agent/cli-darwin-arm64 @sandbox-agent/cli-darwin-x64 @sandbox-agent/cli-win32-x64
173: ```
174: 
175: ```typescript
176: import { SandboxAgent } from "sandbox-agent";
177: 
178: const sdk = await SandboxAgent.start();
179: ```
180: 
181: #### Build from source
182: 
183: If you're running from source instead of the installed CLI.
184: 
185: ```bash
186: cargo run -p sandbox-agent -- server --no-token --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
187: ```
188: 
189: Binding to `0.0.0.0` allows the server to accept connections from any network interface, which is required when running inside a sandbox where clients connect remotely.
190: 
191: #### Configuring token
192: 
193: Tokens are usually not required. Most sandbox providers (E2B, Daytona, etc.) already secure networking at the infrastructure layer.
194: 
195: If you expose the server publicly, use `--token "$SANDBOX_TOKEN"` to require authentication:
196: 
197: ```bash
198: sandbox-agent server --token "$SANDBOX_TOKEN" --host 0.0.0.0 --port 2468
199: ```
200: 
201: Then pass the token when connecting:
202: 
203: #### TypeScript
204: 
205: ```typescript
206: import { SandboxAgent } from "sandbox-agent";
207: 
208: const sdk = await SandboxAgent.connect({
209:   baseUrl: "http://your-server:2468",
210:   token: process.env.SANDBOX_TOKEN,
211: });
212: ```
213: 
214: #### curl
215: 
216: ```bash
217: curl "http://your-server:2468/v1/health" \
218:   -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBOX_TOKEN"
219: ```
220: 
221: #### CLI
222: 
223: ```bash
224: sandbox-agent --token "$SANDBOX_TOKEN" api agents list \
225:   --endpoint http://your-server:2468
226: ```
227: 
228: #### CORS
229: 
230: If you're calling the server from a browser, see the [CORS configuration guide](/cors).
231: 
232: ### Install agents (optional)
233: 
234: To preinstall agents:
235: 
236: ```bash
237: sandbox-agent install-agent --all
238: ```
239: 
240: If agents are not installed up front, they are lazily installed when creating a session.
241: 
242: ### Install desktop dependencies (optional, Linux only)
243: 
244: If you want to use `/v1/desktop/*`, install the desktop runtime packages first:
245: 
246: ```bash
247: sandbox-agent install desktop --yes
248: ```
249: 
250: Then use `GET /v1/desktop/status` or `sdk.getDesktopStatus()` to verify the runtime is ready before calling desktop screenshot or input APIs.
251: 
252: ### Create a session
253: 
254: ```typescript
255: import { SandboxAgent } from "sandbox-agent";
256: 
257: const sdk = await SandboxAgent.connect({
258:   baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:2468",
259: });
260: 
261: const session = await sdk.createSession({
262:   agent: "claude",
263:   sessionInit: {
264:     cwd: "/",
265:     mcpServers: [],
266:   },
267: });
268: 
269: console.log(session.id);
270: ```
271: 
272: ### Send a message
273: 
274: ```typescript
275: const result = await session.prompt([
276:   { type: "text", text: "Summarize the repository and suggest next steps." },
277: ]);
278: 
279: console.log(result.stopReason);
280: ```
281: 
282: ### Read events
283: 
284: ```typescript
285: const off = session.onEvent((event) => {
286:   console.log(event.sender, event.payload);
287: });
288: 
289: const page = await sdk.getEvents({
290:   sessionId: session.id,
291:   limit: 50,
292: });
293: 
294: console.log(page.items.length);
295: off();
296: ```
297: 
298: ### Test with Inspector
299: 
300: Open the Inspector UI at `/ui/` on your server (for example, `http://localhost:2468/ui/`) to inspect sessions and events in a GUI.
301: 
302: ![Sandbox Agent Inspector](https://sandboxagent.dev/docs/images/inspector.png)

2: 
3: > Source: `docs/agent-sessions.mdx`
4: > Canonical URL: https://sandboxagent.dev/docs/agent-sessions
5: > Description: Create sessions, prompt agents, and inspect event history.
6: 
7: ---
8: Sessions are the unit of interaction with an agent. Create one session per task, send prompts, and consume event history.
9: 
10: For SDK-based flows, sessions can be restored after runtime/session loss when persistence is enabled.
11: See [Session Restoration](/session-restoration).
12: 
13: ## Create a session
14: 
15: ```ts
16: import { SandboxAgent } from "sandbox-agent";
17: 
18: const sdk = await SandboxAgent.connect({
19:   baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:2468",
20: });
21: 
22: const session = await sdk.createSession({
23:   agent: "codex",
24:   cwd: "/",
25: });
26: 
27: console.log(session.id, session.agentSessionId);
28: ```
29: 
30: ## Send a prompt
31: 
32: ```ts
33: const response = await session.prompt([
34:   { type: "text", text: "Summarize the repository structure." },
35: ]);
36: 
37: console.log(response.stopReason);
38: ```
39: 
40: ## Subscribe to live events
41: 
42: ```ts
43: const unsubscribe = session.onEvent((event) => {
44:   console.log(event.eventIndex, event.sender, event.payload);
45: });
46: 
47: await session.prompt([
48:   { type: "text", text: "Explain the main entrypoints." },
49: ]);
50: 
51: unsubscribe();
52: ```
53: 
54: ### Event types
55: 
56: Each event's `payload` contains a session update. The `sessionUpdate` field identifies the type.
57: 
58: #### agent_message_chunk
59: 
60: Streamed text or content from the agent's response.
61: 
62: ```json
63: {
64:   "sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk",
65:   "content": { "type": "text", "text": "Here's how the repository is structured..." }
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: #### agent_thought_chunk
70: 
71: Internal reasoning from the agent (chain-of-thought / extended thinking).
72: 
73: ```json
74: {
75:   "sessionUpdate": "agent_thought_chunk",
76:   "content": { "type": "text", "text": "I should start by looking at the project structure..." }
77: }
78: ```
79: 
80: #### user_message_chunk
81: 
82: Echo of the user's prompt being processed.
83: 
84: ```json
85: {
86:   "sessionUpdate": "user_message_chunk",
87:   "content": { "type": "text", "text": "Summarize the repository structure." }
88: }
89: ```
90: 
91: #### tool_call
92: 
93: The agent invoked a tool (file edit, terminal command, etc.).
94: 
95: ```json
96: {
97:   "sessionUpdate": "tool_call",
98:   "toolCallId": "tc_abc123",
99:   "title": "Read file",
100:   "status": "in_progress",
101:   "rawInput": { "path": "/src/index.ts" }
102: }
103: ```
104: 
105: #### tool_call_update
106: 
107: Progress or result update for an in-progress tool call.
108: 
109: ```json
110: {
111:   "sessionUpdate": "tool_call_update",
112:   "toolCallId": "tc_abc123",
113:   "status": "completed",
114:   "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "import express from 'express';\n..." }]
115: }
116: ```
117: 
118: #### plan
119: 
120: The agent's execution plan for the current task.
121: 
122: ```json
123: {
124:   "sessionUpdate": "plan",
125:   "entries": [
126:     { "content": "Read the project structure", "status": "completed" },
127:     { "content": "Identify main entrypoints", "status": "in_progress" },
128:     { "content": "Write summary", "status": "pending" }
129:   ]
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: #### usage_update
134: 
135: Token usage metrics for the current turn.
136: 
137: ```json
138: {
139:   "sessionUpdate": "usage_update"
140: }
141: ```
142: 
143: #### session_info_update
144: 
145: Session metadata changed (e.g. agent-generated title).
146: 
147: ```json
148: {
149:   "sessionUpdate": "session_info_update",
150:   "title": "Repository structure analysis"
151: }
152: ```
153: 
154: ## Fetch persisted event history
155: 
156: ```ts
157: const page = await sdk.getEvents({
158:   sessionId: session.id,
159:   limit: 50,
160: });
161: 
162: for (const event of page.items) {
163:   console.log(event.id, event.createdAt, event.sender);
164: }
165: ```
166: 
167: ## List and load sessions
168: 
169: ```ts
170: const sessions = await sdk.listSessions({ limit: 20 });
171: 
172: for (const item of sessions.items) {
173:   console.log(item.id, item.agent, item.createdAt);
174: }
175: 
176: if (sessions.items.length > 0) {
177:   const loaded = await sdk.resumeSession(sessions.items[0]!.id);
178:   await loaded.prompt([{ type: "text", text: "Continue." }]);
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: ## Configure model, mode, and thought level
183: 
184: Set the model, mode, or thought level on a session at creation time or after:
185: 
186: ```ts
187: // At creation time
188: const session = await sdk.createSession({
189:   agent: "codex",
190:   model: "gpt-5.3-codex",
191:   mode: "auto",
192:   thoughtLevel: "high",
193: });
194: ```
195: 
196: ```ts
197: // After creation
198: await session.setModel("gpt-5.2-codex");
199: await session.setMode("full-access");
200: await session.setThoughtLevel("medium");
201: ```
202: 
203: Query available modes:
204: 
205: ```ts
206: const modes = await session.getModes();
207: console.log(modes?.currentModeId, modes?.availableModes);
208: ```
209: 
210: ### Advanced config options
211: 
212: For config options beyond model, mode, and thought level, use `getConfigOptions` to discover what the agent supports and `setConfigOption` to set any option by ID:
213: 
214: ```ts
215: const options = await session.getConfigOptions();
216: for (const opt of options) {
217:   console.log(opt.id, opt.category, opt.type);
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: ```ts
222: await session.setConfigOption("some-agent-option", "value");
223: ```
224: 
225: ## Handle permission requests
226: 
227: For agents that request tool-use permissions, register a permission listener and reply with `once`, `always`, or `reject`:
228: 
229: ```ts
230: const session = await sdk.createSession({
231:   agent: "claude",
232:   mode: "default",
233: });
234: 
235: session.onPermissionRequest((request) => {
236:   console.log(request.toolCall.title, request.availableReplies);
237:   void session.respondPermission(request.id, "once");
238: });
239: 
240: await session.prompt([
241:   { type: "text", text: "Create ./permission-example.txt with the text hello." },
242: ]);
243: ```
244: 
245: ### Auto-approving permissions
246: 
247: To auto-approve all permission requests, respond with `"once"` or `"always"` in your listener:
248: 
249: ```ts
250: session.onPermissionRequest((request) => {
251:   void session.respondPermission(request.id, "always");
252: });
253: ```
254: 
255: See `examples/permissions/src/index.ts` for a complete permissions example that works with Claude and Codex.
256: 
257: Some agents like Claude allow configuring permission behavior through modes (e.g. `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`). We recommend leaving the mode as `default` and handling permission decisions explicitly in `onPermissionRequest` instead.
258: 
259: ## Destroy a session
260:

41:   cwd,
42: });
